changes: Added include_flagged ID 3581 for How AI Agents Discover Scientific Equations: From Hydrotope Rediscovery to New Water-Wave Amplitudes. The source reports: a PI/two-student agent team produced a new independent analytic expression for the six-point, three-negative-wavenumber deep-water surface-wave amplitude; the expression passed 140 exact tests in 58 chambers, but the paper supplies no analytic proof. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00435v1. Further checking: establish the formula's exact domain, novelty and priority; obtain an analytic proof or independent symbolic derivation beyond the reported finite exact tests; verify every chamber and separate the rediscovery experiments from the genuinely new three-minus expression. No supplied run record or computation was executed here.

Added include_flagged ID 3582 for A Proof of the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture. The source reports: a proof of the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture: there is an absolute integer C such that every K_t-minor-free graph is Ct-colorable. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05291v1. Further checking: obtain independent graph-theory review of Theorems 4 and 5 and the reduction to the full conjecture; verify novelty and all imported hypotheses; check that the reported Lean development covers the paper and every external input; reconstruct the model/author contribution trace. The Lean artifact was not executed here.

Added include_flagged ID 3583 for A simple construction of a simple nil ring. The source reports: The paper presents a substantially simplified construction/proof that over every countable field there exists a simple associative nil algebra, a theorem first established by Smoktunowicz. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05384v1. Further checking: independently verify the ring construction and claimed substantial simplification; identify Aristotle (Harmonic), the exact ChatGPT model and their respective mathematical roles; check priority against other simplifications and ensure the contribution is more than a rediscovery or exposition of the 1999 proof.

Added include_flagged ID 3584 for A Fraction Dimensional Kakeya Compression. The source reports: an explicit curved-Kakeya family in R^3 satisfying the Hoermander condition and failing worst compression whose union has Hausdorff and upper box dimension 5/2, answering a question in arXiv:2607.27629. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05404v1. Further checking: independently verify the Hoermander condition, failure of worst compression and both dimension bounds; compare the construction and scope with the acknowledged concurrent work; establish novelty/priority and the exact human/model allocation.

Added include_flagged ID 3585 for Amicable numbers. The source reports: the upper bound A(x) <= x exp{-(1/2+o(1)) log x log_3 x / log_2 x} for the count of amicable numbers up to x, described as the first bound of the expected shape. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05661v1. Further checking: independently verify the analytic-number-theory argument, constant 1/2 and novelty; check the reported Lean theorem statement, source correspondence, dependencies and kernel result without trusting the source's self-report. The formalization was not executed here.

Added include_flagged ID 3586 for Pathological viscosity solutions of Hamilton--Jacobi equations. The source reports: a continuous u on the closed unit ball in R^4 and a smooth autonomous H:R^4->[1,2] for which the same u is a viscosity solution of H(Du)=c for every c in [1,2]. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05736v1. Further checking: independently verify the construction, viscosity-solution quantifiers and dimension-four scope; check novelty and whether lower dimensions remain open; reconstruct the mathematical contribution boundary from the interaction record if one becomes public.

Added include_flagged ID 3587 for Moment estimates for chaoses with regular moment growth. The source reports: two-sided moment estimates for decoupled chaoses of arbitrary order with independent symmetric variables of regular moment growth, plus tail bounds and explicit Rademacher and Weibull formulae. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05829v1. Further checking: independently verify the upper bound in arbitrary order, the extension from log-concave tails to regular moment growth, constants and novelty; determine which proof steps were model-generated and whether the vague assistance statement reflects a material mathematical role.

Added include_flagged ID 3588 for Golod--Shafarevich for arithmetic surfaces. The source reports: Golod-Shafarevich towers of arithmetic surfaces over the integers, yielding an arithmetic surface with section and infinite geometric etale fundamental group, curves over Q with infinite geometric etale towers in which a rational point splits completely, and a sequence with logarithmic conductor growing at most linearly with genus. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06461v1. Further checking: obtain specialist review of the arithmetic-surface construction, obstruction estimates and all three claimed answers; compare the simultaneous/concurrent literature; verify novelty, statement correspondence and the precise contribution of each model and author.

Added include_flagged ID 3589 for Poly and Raby's theorem splits in infinite dimensions. The source reports: in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces C^k smoothness of squared distance characterizes weakly C^k submanifolds, while C^k submanifolds require an additional pointwise equicontinuity condition; it supplies a tight counterexample separating the notions. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06595v1. Further checking: independently verify Example 4.1, the weak-C^k characterization, the pointwise-equicontinuity criterion and claimed novelty; inspect the interaction record if available to map the AI contribution beyond the explicit example.

Added include_flagged ID 3590 for Erdős 1139: large gaps between almost-primes. The source reports: unconditional Lean proofs that the normalized gap limsup for consecutive P_2 almost-primes is at least a constant A>1 and that every sufficiently large X contains a P_2-free interval of length at least c log X for a fixed c>1, plus the stated CRT, primorial and squared-core reductions. The full infinite-limsup conjecture is only conditional on an explicit Green–Tao–Ziegler linear-forms premise, and the repository also proves a reverse implication from that premise to prime arithmetic progressions of arbitrary length. Primary source: https://github.com/linrock/math-proofs/commit/38ad7ea8de1efe526f665c2b5204465e5ed879fe. Further checking: Independently establish novelty and priority of the unconditional strict limsup >1 and uniform c>1 bounds against Chojecki (Erdős 689), the June 2026 Chojecki–Price–Sherry–Tao candidate proof, and any intervening literature; obtain a claim-level account of the unidentified agent's mathematical contribution; have a number theorist check the formal/informal statement correspondence and the explicit Green–Tao–Ziegler premise; and independently replay the pinned proof package. Do not describe the full infinite-limsup conjecture as unconditionally proved.

Added include_flagged ID 3591 for S(6) ≤ 1801 if R₄(3) ≤ 61: a centred Schur bound and the structure at the frontier. The source reports: a general centred implication R_k(3)≤r => S(k+1)≤2(k+1) floor((r-1)/2)+1, giving S(3)≤13 and, under the explicit unproved premise R_4(3)≤61, S(6)≤1801, together with exact frontier-structure theorems. It explicitly does not prove R_4(3)≤61 or S(6)≤1800. Primary source: https://github.com/mysticflounder/schur-centred-bound/commit/6b1c69732d73428042efce8d563f67604320cad4. Further checking: Independently review all fourteen compared statements and the transfer from Ramsey to Schur bounds; verify the external R_4(3)≤61 claim and its certificates separately because this repository treats it only as a hypothesis; compare the claimed centred method and frontier theorems against the inaccessible full texts of Wan and Li and the wider literature; document the exact ChatGPT/Claude/human contribution split; and preserve the conditional wording and the explicit non-claim S(6)≤1800.

Added include_flagged ID 3592 for FluidSingularSets. The source reports: Hausdorff nullity for every finite product of squared successive-logarithm gauges and an upper parabolic box-dimension bound 25/23 for compact interior singular sets of unforced three-dimensional suitable weak Navier–Stokes solutions. Primary source: https://github.com/CoolRmal/FluidSingularSets/commit/dd3ae61ce421a634818f52a6e11a8b78dd1bfc97. Further checking: Obtain independent PDE-specialist review of both source manuscripts and the exact gauge and localization definitions; establish novelty/priority for the finite successive-log family and 25/23 bound; audit claim-level GPT-6 versus human contribution; check formal/informal statement correspondence and the reused CKN dependency; and independently replay the pinned package.

Added include_flagged ID 3593 for The Schur degree of block sums: L(4)=16 and L(5)≥49. The source reports: Lean proofs L(4)=16 and 49≤L(5)≤65, a lift from sumfree group partitions to block-sum sequences, and thereby counterexamples at n=4 and n=5 to Eliahou–Revuelta's conjecture L(n)=S(n-1)+1. The paper's external upper bound is 61, while the Lean development proves only 65 via R_4(3)≤66. Primary source: https://github.com/mysticflounder/schur-degree-block-sums/commit/933000c135141347835300ca13b3a15ff050d03a. Further checking: Seek independent additive-combinatorics review; reproduce the finite and group-partition checks outside this evidence lane; reconcile the paper's L(5)≤61 with the formally certified L(5)≤65 and audit the adaptation of prior source theorems; establish priority/novelty; document the exact human/Claude contribution; and independently replay and align the formal statements.

Added include_flagged ID 3594 for Structured orthogonal and unitary matrices: factorization, geometry and singularities. The source reports: two- and three-layer orthogonal/unitary factorization results, explicit four-layer counterexamples, exact two-factor cell-rank and cosine-sine exhaustion results, shared-orbit differential geometry, and genuine topological singularities for all real q≥3 and odd unitary q≥3. It excludes experimental special-unitary drafts and the listed remaining problems. Primary source: https://github.com/alialiev78/gs_Lean_formalization/commit/1270ba6cf3050f53a4beb98f0d65ab7459d4494b. Further checking: Resolve the Palomar warning by reconciling the public build guide with the submitted toolchain and mathlib revision; independently verify the sixteen selected statements and formal/informal correspondence; determine which unitary, singularity and shared-geometry extensions are new relative to arXiv:2609.27982 and other literature; document claim-level ChatGPT/human allocation and the historical model; and independently replay the pinned package.

Updated existing ID 275 (Parity of the partition function in quadratic progressions): claim_and_formalization_scope_expansion. Further checking: Independently verify Corollary 2 and replay the pinned PartitionParity and PartitionZheng Lean developments; check manuscript-to-formal-statement correspondence and all designated classical hypotheses; verify the v3-to-v4 change set; and keep clear that the Lean artifacts omit the Borcherds-lift/divisor construction, characteristic-2 geometry, parity-elimination arguments and propagation theorem. Clarify whether AxiomProver contributed to discovery or only formalized author-supplied arguments. Keep provisional=1, unreviewed, conservative confidence and no Superhuman override. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.09553v4.

Further checking: Independently replay the exact verifier, audit the certificate/configuration and search provenance, establish novelty and priority, and resolve the remaining open interval; keep provisional=1, unreviewed, conservative confidence and no Superhuman override. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14013v2.
